- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast lows.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); apply dampening factor of 0.85–0.90 to post-spike forecasts.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; force mean reversion toward 3–5 day moving average of prior 10–15 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to over-predict late-period values (last 7–10 days); cap forecast decline after day 20–25 unless sentiment supports continuation.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), model often misreads trend; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day price and sentiment to anchor forecast midpoints.
